hn.originalTitle: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its Workspace MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email | Tech Stackups

On 24 November, Google made its eight Workspace MCP servers generally available and published a new clause in its API terms. From 1 February 2027, any tool that "is or is driven by an AI Agent" must reach Gmail, Drive, Calendar and the rest of Workspace through those servers.

Read the Gmail server's tool list and you'll find that it can search your mail, read threads, create a draft and file things under labels. It can't send a message, reply, forward, or change a draft after creating it. Those tools exist, but Google's quota page says they "require partner access and aren't generally available".

If you've built an email assistant on the Gmail API, or you run a coding agent with a Google Workspace plugin, you have about two months to work out which side of the rule you're on.

What the rule says ​

The new Workspace AI Tools Addendum to the Google APIs puts it in one sentence:

The GWS Access Tool must use a Google MCP where the GWS Access Tool is or is driven by an AI Agent, an AI Harness or an AI model or service employing an AI model.

The next sentence forbids disguising an agent to avoid the classification. Breaking either lets Google "restrict or remove the GWS Access Tool's access" or suspend your account.

There's a technical side too. From the same date, agents that call the REST APIs directly are held to Standard-tier quotas , whatever tier the project has paid for. REST keeps working for them, slowly and in breach of the terms.

Apps that don't involve AI carry on as before. A nightly backup job, a CRM sync or a deterministic script on its own OAuth client is, in Google's words, "not affected by this change".

The addendum also adds data rules that matter to anyone building an agent with memory:

Workspace data may only be processed "to fulfill active, user-authorized tasks", and must be deleted when the user disconnects.

Google can cap retention of what it calls "Google Technical Information" at 30 days. Its definition includes vector embeddings, memory indexes, user profiles and organisational graphs built from Workspace data.

Training, fine-tuning, evals and distillation on the data are banned, as is using it to build a competing Workspace product.

The 30-day cap is the one product teams will feel. An assistant that builds a long-term index of your inbox to answer questions about last year's contracts has to rebuild it monthly or drop it.

What the MCP servers can do ​

Coverage is uneven. Docs, Slides and Tasks are close to everything the REST API offers. Gmail and Drive are much thinner.

The Gmail gap is the one that breaks real workflows. An agent that drafts a reply, gets feedback from you and revises it before you hit send can't do the revision step. It has to create a second draft and leave the first one behind.

Drive's gap is similar: an agent can create a report but can't move it into the right folder or share it with the team.

Partners get more ​

Google hasn't said who qualifies for partner access or when the partner-only Gmail tools will reach everyone. The effect is already visible, though. Anthropic's Google Workspace connector for Claude advertises sending, replying and forwarding email, and moving and trashing Drive files. Those are exactly the operations the public servers lack.

So a large AI vendor's agent can send your email through an approved channel, while an independent developer's agent, using the same OAuth scopes the user granted, can only leave drafts. Once the addendum takes effect, that independent developer also can't fall back to the REST API without breaching the terms.

Who counts as an agent ​

The definitions are broad. An "AI Harness" or a tool "driven by" an AI model plausibly covers a personal script that pipes your inbox into an LLM, and a "GWS Access Point" explicitly includes any "connector, proxy, command line interface, or third-party service". Google hasn't addressed hobby use directly.

Classification starts with self-declaration. OAuth clients now have a checkbox, "Use this client for an AI-powered agent", and since 11 November the MCP servers reject clients without it. Clients created before the cut-off and not marked in time stay non-agentic permanently, so owners have to create new ones. Google hasn't said how it will detect agents that call REST without declaring themselves.

A few edge cases are documented:

Service accounts with domain-wide delegation can't set the agentic flag. Their MCP requests aren't rejected for missing it, but still trigg
hn.titleZh: 谷歌將讓 AI 代理使用其 MCP 伺服器。 Gmail無法傳送郵件
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 MCP / Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
谷歌将让 AI 代理使用其 Workspace MCP 服务器。 Gmail 無法發送電子郵件 |技術堆疊 11 月 24 日，Google 全面開放其八台 Workspace MCP 伺服器，並在其 API 條款中發布了一項新條款。從 2027 年 2 月 1 日起，任何「由 AI 代理程式驅動」的工具都必須透過這些伺服器存取 Gmail、雲端硬碟、日曆和 Workspace 的其餘部分。閱讀 Gmail 伺服器的工具列表，您會發現它可以搜尋郵件、閱讀線程、建立草稿以及在標籤下歸檔內容。建立草稿後，它無法發送訊息、回覆、轉發或更改草稿。這些工具是存在的，但Google的配額頁面稱它們「需要合作夥伴訪問，並且一般不可用」。如果您在 Gmail API 上建立了電子郵件助手，或者使用 Google Workspace 外掛程式運行編碼代理，那麼您有大約兩個月的時間來確定自己站在規則的哪一邊。規則內容Google API 的新 Workspace AI 工具附錄用一句話概括了這一點：GWS 存取工具必須使用 Google MCP，其中 GWS 存取工具由 AI 代理、AI 線束或採用 AI 模型的 AI 模型或服務驅動。下一句禁止偽裝代理以避免分類。如果違反，Google 將「限製或刪除 GWS 存取工具的存取權限」或暫停您的帳戶。還有技術方面。

從同一天起，直接呼叫 REST API 的代理將受到標準層配額的限制，無論專案支付了多少層費用。 REST 繼續為他們工作，緩慢且違反條款。不涉及人工智慧的應用程式會像以前一樣繼續運作。用 Google 的話來說，夜間備份作業、CRM 同步或 OAuth 用戶端上的確定性腳本「不受此變更的影響」。該附錄還添加了對任何構建具有內存的代理的人都很重要的數據規則：工作區數據只能被處理“以完成活動的、用戶授權的任務”，並且必須在用戶斷開連接時刪除。 Google 可以將所謂的「Google 技術資訊」的保留期限限制為 30 天。其定義包括向量嵌入、記憶體索引、使用者設定檔和根據工作區資料建構的組織圖。禁止對資料進行訓練、微調、評估和蒸餾，就像使用它來建立競爭性工作區產品一樣。產品團隊會感受到 30 天的上限。為您的收件匣建立長期索引以回答有關去年合約的問題的助理必須每月重建或放棄它。 MCP伺服器可以做什麼覆蓋範圍參差不齊。文件、投影片和任務接近 REST API 提供的所有功能。 Gmail 和 Drive 較薄。 Gmail 的差距是真正破壞工作流程的一個因素。

在您點擊發送之前起草回复、從您那裡獲取反饋並進行修改的代理無法執行修改步驟。它必須制定第二稿並留下第一稿。 Drive 的差距類似：代理可以建立報告，但無法將其移至正確的資料夾或與團隊共用。合作夥伴獲得更多Google 尚未說明誰有資格獲得合作夥伴存取權限，也沒有說明合作夥伴專用的 Gmail 工具何時會惠及所有人。不過，效果已經可見。 Anthropic 的 Claude Google Workspace 連接器宣傳發送、回覆和轉發電子郵件，以及移動和刪除雲端硬碟檔案。這些正是公共伺服器所缺乏的操作。因此，大型 AI 供應商的代理商可以透過核准的管道發送您的電子郵件，而獨立開發人員的代理商則使用使用者授予的相同 OAuth 範圍，只能留下草稿。一旦附錄生效，獨立開發人員也無法在不違反條款的情況下退回 REST API。誰算是代理人定義很廣泛。 「AI Harness」或「由 AI 模型驅動」的工具似乎涵蓋了將您的收件匣傳輸到 LLM 的個人腳本，而「GWS 存取點」明確包含任何「連接器、代理程式、命令列介面或第三方服務」。谷歌尚未直接解決愛好使用問題。分類從自我聲明開始。

OAuth 用戶端現在有一個複選框“將此客戶端用作 AI 支援的代理”，自 11 月 11 日起，MCP 伺服器拒絕沒有該複選框的客戶端。在截止時間之前建立且未及時標記的用戶端將永久保持非代理狀態，因此擁有者必須建立新客戶端。 Google 尚未說明如何偵測在未宣告自身的情況下呼叫 REST 的代理程式。記錄了一些邊緣情況：具有網域範圍委派的服務帳戶無法設定代理標誌。他們的 MCP 請求不會因錯過而被拒絕，但仍會觸發

hn.sourceOriginalText:
AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp  | devnull.land

tl;dr — I recommend using llama-cpp-rdna-boosts if you have an AMD graphics card. It’s lean, and increased my token generation from 35 to 55 tokens/second, and my prefill from 700 to 1300 tokens per second. YMMV.

As of November 2026, an explosion in the number of bespoke inference engines has taken place. Many of them take inspiration from the engines that enabled much of the LLM inference up 'til now: llama.cpp, SGLang, vLLM, etc.

The rationale isn’t that those options are bad, but merely that they are generalist engines, optimized for no particular hardware and with a focus on broad compatibility. Others feel the development pace of those engines have slowed down, and with the help of LLMs, they can move faster on their own.

Some examples of these new inference engines* are Strata, Basalt, RustingStrata, etc…

These new forks generally all have a few things in common:

They focus on a specific subset of models and/or hardware

They use a frontier model to vibe-code the entire thing

They chase ever-higher token generation speeds

… and the results are stunning! Strata is able to run a heavily-quantized model of Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 180B parameter model , on a 16GB VRAM graphics card, and 16GB system RAM, and have it generate tokens at a surprisingly high rate.

In and of itself those three things are not red flags (the second is concerning, of course, but it may be SOP in a year’s time — who knows!), but as these projects have evolved, that relentless chase toward higher token generation speeds has taken an unfortunate turn, in that the optimizations are less about hardware-specific changes, but more about changing how the model thinks so that it goes brrr faster.

Strata specifically has taken to preferring to poll experts loaded in VRAM even if other experts (pushed to system RAM/disk) would have been normally chosen. This is just one example, but certainly not the last.

That said, I was fortunate to stumble upon yet another project that promised improvements, delivered, and was more aligned with my software development philosophy.

Enter llama-cpp-rdna-boosts . It is a repository that contains a minimal set of changes that you apply against a pinned commit of llama.cpp. It is in essence a fork, but one whose changeset is continually re-applied to newer versions of llama.cpp. It contains AMD-specific improvements that drastically improve prefill and token-generation speeds.

I appreciate llama.cpp’s approach to software development. They are a stable base to branch off from. Contributions are vetted throughly and applied judiciously. ✅

The rdna-boosts repo is a set of small patches that are applied to base llama.cpp. Fewer moving parts mean fewer things to maintain ✅

The changes are (somewhat opaquely, it’s all straight Claudish 😬) outlined in the documentation, ensuring some degree of transparency. ✅

If you have ROCm libraries installed on your system, you can build the image yourself. I didn’t want to mess with that, so I used the pre-built images published.

podman pull ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1

This sets up an image that you can run sandboxed via podman to launch the inference server:

podman run --rm -it \ --network=host \ --device /dev/kfd \ --device /dev/dri \ --group-add video \ -v "$HOME/models:/models" \ "ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1" \ My actual launch script passes a few additional flags, but those are the important lines.

I imagine upgrading would be pulling a new image down, though I have not tried this yet.

On my setup, an AMD R9700 connected to my laptop via an eGPU interface, this improved prefill and token generation rates when running ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_L) with MTP enabled:

Strata and its ilk were always promising the moon and it was never clear what steps they took to make that happen. I’m very much looking forward to what the rdna-boosts community come up with next.

* It’s worth noting that between these two groups, vllm-radiance made an appearance, which was a fork of vLLM with AMD-specific patches. I tried this too, but the build steps were so onerous and vLLM so overbuilt for my specific use case (1 machine, 1 developer), that I abandoned it and went back to vanilla llama.cpp

hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 AI Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
AMD 专用的 llama.cpp 分支 | devnull.land tl;dr — 如果您有 AMD 显卡，我建议使用 llama-cpp-rdna-boosts。它很精简，将我的代币生成从 35 个代币/秒增加到 55 个代币/秒，并将我的预填充从每秒 700 个代币增加到 1300 个代币。 YMMV。截至 2026 年 11 月，定制推理引擎的数量出现爆炸式增长。其中許多都從迄今為止支援大部分 LLM 推理的引擎中汲取靈感：llama.cpp、SGLang、vLLM 等。其理由并不是这些选项不好，而仅仅是因为它们是通用引擎，针对没有特定硬件进行了优化，并且注重广泛的兼容性。其他人則認為這些引擎的開發速度已經放緩，在法學碩士的幫助下，他們可以自己更快地前進。这些新推理引擎*的一些例子是 Strata、Basalt、RustingStrata 等……这些新分叉通常都有一些共同点：它们专注于模型和/或硬件的特定子集它们使用前沿模型对整个事物进行振动编码它们追求更高的代币生成速度……结果令人惊叹！ Strata 能够在 16GB VRAM 显卡和 16GB 系统 RAM 上运行 Qwen 3.8 Flash Next 的高度量化模型（180B 参数模型），并以惊人的高速率生成代币。

就其本身而言，這三件事並不是危險信號（當然，第二件事令人擔憂，但它可能會在一年後成為 SOP——誰知道呢！），但隨著這些項目的發展，對更高代幣生成速度的不懈追求發生了不幸的轉變，因為優化不再是針對特定於硬體的變化，而是更多地關於改變模型的思維方式，使其運行得更快。 Strata 特別傾向於輪詢 VRAM 中載入的專家，即使通常會選擇其他專家（推送到系統 RAM/磁碟）。這只是一個例子，但肯定不是最後一個。也就是說，我很幸運地偶然發現了另一個項目，它承諾改進、交付，並且更符合我的軟體開發理念。输入 llama-cpp-rdna-boosts 。它是一個儲存庫，包含您對 llama.cpp 的固定提交應用的最小更改集。它本質上是一個分支，但其變更集不斷地重新應用於較新版本的 llama.cpp。它包含 AMD 特定的改進，可顯著提高預填充和令牌生成速度。我很欣赏 llama.cpp 的软件开发方法。它们是一个稳定的分支基础。捐款均经过彻底审查并明智应用。 ✅ rdna-boosts 儲存庫是一組應用於基礎 llama.cpp 的小補丁。

更少的移動部件意味著更少的維護工作 ✅ 這些更改（有點不透明，都是直接 Claudish 😬）在文件中概述，確保了一定程度的透明度。 ✅ 如果您的系統上安裝了 ROCm 庫，您可以自行建立映像。我不想搞亂它，所以我使用了發布的預建圖像。 podman pull ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1 這會設定一個映像，您可以透過 podman 在沙盒中執行該映像以啟動推理伺服器： podman run --rm -it \ --network=host \ --device /dev/deo \ --device /dev/dm \ --device /dev/deo/dri --device \devvid -device /dev/k/ "$HOME/models:/models" \ "ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1" \ 我的實際啟動腳本傳遞了一些額外的標誌，但這些是重要的行。我想升級會拉下一個新的圖像，儘管我還沒有嘗試過。在我的設定中，AMD R9700 透過 eGPU 介面連接到我的筆記型電腦，在啟用 MTP 的情況下運行 ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_L) 時，這提高了預填充和令牌生成率：Strata 及其同類承諾登月，但不清楚實現他們總是採取了哪些目標。我非常期待 rdna-boosts 社區下一步的成果。

* 值得注意的是，在這兩組之間，vllm-radiance 出現了，它是 vLLM 的一個分支，帶有 AMD 特定的補丁。我也嘗試過這個，但是構建步驟非常繁重，而且 vLLM 對於我的特定用例（1 台機器，1 名開發人員）來說過度構建，所以我放棄了它並返回到 vanilla llama.cpp ← 返回所有帖子

hn.originalTitle: AI agents now control part of DeepMind's compute for Gemini experiments
hn.sourceOriginalText:
AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant

AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant

Google Deepmind lets AI agents run experiments on their own for the next Gemini model. On the company's podcast, VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu, who leads Gemini development, frames this as part of a strategic shift at the lab. Rather than running separate teams for specialized projects like AlphaFold and nuclear fusion, Deepmind now relies on a single general-purpose algorithm for both science and products, he says. Each Gemini generation, he adds, is a hand-built one-off rather than a fixed architecture, while parallel teams work on its successors.

According to Kavukcuoglu, AI agents control part of the compute themselves to run experiments, though the lab is still far from full recursive self-improvement. As a safety measure, Deepmind doesn't reward the agents' internal thought streams ("Chain of Thought") during training, he says, so their intentions stay unfiltered and reviewable in natural language before they act.

Kavukcuoglu also points to limits. Today's AI can depict physical processes such as fluid flows and collisions with visual accuracy, he says, but doesn't understand them precisely. No test can show when models will close those gaps and reach artificial general intelligence (AGI), he argues, because no benchmark captures the core of intelligence. In his view, AGI won't begin until useful everyday products earn enough trust for people to hand decisions over to them, the way they would when working with other people. Ad Ad

hn.sourceTextZh:
AI 代理現在控制 Deepmind 對 Gemini 實驗的部分計算，但遞歸自我改進仍然遙遠 AI 代理現在控制 Deepmind 對 Gemini 實驗的部分計算，但遞歸自我改進仍然遙遠 Google Deepmind 讓 AI 代理為下一個 Gemini 模型自行運行實驗。在該公司的播客中，負責 Gemini 開發的研究副總裁 Koray Kavukcuoglu 將此視為實驗室策略轉變的一部分。他說，Deepmind 現在不再為 AlphaFold 和核融合等專門專案運行單獨的團隊，而是在科學和產品方面依賴單一通用的演算法。他補充道，每一代 Gemini 都是手工構建的一次性架構，而不是固定的架構，而平行團隊則致力於開發其後繼產品。 Kavukcuoglu 表示，人工智慧代理自己控制部分計算來運行實驗，儘管實驗室距離完全遞歸自我改進還很遠。他說，作為一項安全措施，Deepmind 在訓練期間不會獎勵智能體的內部思維流（「思維鏈」），因此他們的意圖在行動之前不會被過濾並可以用自然語言進行審查。卡武克措格魯也指出了限制。他說，今天的人工智慧可以視覺精度描述流體流動和碰撞等物理過程，但不能準確地理解它們。

他認為，沒有任何測試可以表明模型何時能夠彌合這些差距並達到通用人工智慧（AGI），因為沒有任何基準能夠抓住智慧的核心。在他看來，只有有用的日常產品贏得足夠的信任，讓人們將決策權交給他們，就像他們與其他人合作時一樣，AGI 才會開始。沒有炒作的廣告廣告 AI 新聞 – 由 Humans Every Plus 文章和完整存檔前沿雷達策劃：每年 6 次深入研究 已經是訂閱者？登入

hn.sourceOriginalText:
Google gives AI agents 69 days to move to Workspace MCP · Vortner

Google gives AI agents 69 days to move to Workspace MCP

The AI can read the inbox , but only draft emails .

MCP is also the one path to Workspace data that Google bills from the first request on its paid tier.

Disclosure: I build Vortner, a permission layer between company tools and AI clients. Google's new rules impact products like mine, which is why I read all of them. Nothing below depends on that. Every number comes from Google's own pages or from public package registries, and the method is at the end.

On November 24, Google made its Workspace MCP servers generally available, introduced two usage tiers and published a Workspace AI Tools Addendum . The core rule, from the announcement : agents "must use MCP to access Workspace data, rather than calling Workspace REST APIs directly". Technical enforcement starts February 1, 2027.

Some of what came with it is good. External agents have to identify themselves in OAuth, so admins can manage them like any other app. Admins can set rules that make users confirm sensitive actions, agent actions show up in audit logs, and existing DLP rules apply when someone uses an agent. If you've seen a prompt injection talk an agent into forwarding a mailbox, you want all of that.

None of it needed the mandate or the meter, though. Agent identity is a checkbox on the OAuth client, "Use this client for an AI-powered agent", which Google's help page calls a self-declaration. It would work the same way on REST. Audit logs and DLP run on Google's side either way. The confirmation prompts are the only control that needs a hook in the protocol, and that could have been an admin setting along the lines of "agents in my org must use MCP". So I looked at what the mandate and the pricing do on their own.

The path agents must take is the only one without a free allowance

Workspace now has a free Standard tier and a paid Scaled tier. On Scaled, REST traffic gets a daily no-charge allowance per billing account: 70 million Light, 10 million Medium and 1 million Premium Gmail requests, with similar allowances for Drive and Calendar. You only pay above that. MCP on Scaled has no allowance at all. From April 1, 2027, every successful MCP request is billed, and the 5,000 free MCP requests a day you had on Standard go away when you move up.

There's also an internal-use exception that lets a company's own projects get higher REST quotas without paying. It doesn't cover MCP . A company that builds its own agent for its own mailboxes pays per call on top of its Workspace licences as soon as it outgrows the free 5,000 requests a day, while a plain script reading the same mailboxes doesn't.

What a basic email assistant costs

The free Standard tier caps MCP at 5,000 requests per day, per project, per product, shared by everyone on that project. Most Gmail MCP tools count as one request. search_threads and list_drafts count as ten, because they make several calls underneath. That makes the free tier 500 email searches a day for the whole project. Google's quota pages also say failed tool calls are billed, because they come back as HTTP 200 with an error flag. REST billing only counts successful responses.

To see what this means in practice, I modelled a modest assistant: 5 searches, 15 thread reads and 3 drafts per person per workday. That's 68 units per person, so 73 people use up the free tier. On Scaled, at Google's prices (searching and reading a thread are both Premium, $0.50 per 1,000), it comes to $0.73 per person per month.

That's $364 a month for 500 people and $3,641 for 5,000. Over REST, the same calls would cost nothing until about 43,000 people, even if every call were billed at the Premium rate. The workload is my guess. Plug in your own and the gap stays the same shape.

To be fair to Google, these are small amounts, and nobody goes broke at $0.73 a head. The problem is the structure: the path agents are required to use is the one where the meter runs from the first call, and the company running the meter also decides which tools exist on that path. In Gmail's MCP, sending, replying and forwarding currently need partner access and aren't generally available.

On May 1 , Google opened the Workspace MCP server as a public developer preview and pitched MCP as a standard way for agents to get context and tools. There was no requirement. The same post promised owners of existing projects at least 60 days' notice before quota changes. Google's tools-safety page, now folded into the usa

hn.sourceTextZh:
Google 給 AI 代理 69 天的時間遷移到 Workspace MCP · Vortner Google 給 AI 代理 69 天的時間遷移到 Workspace MCP AI 可以閱讀收件箱，但只能草擬電子郵件。 MCP 也是 Google 從其付費層的第一個請求開始計費的 Workspace 資料的唯一途徑。揭露：我建立了 Vortner，這是公司工具和 AI 用戶端之間的權限層。谷歌的新規則影響了像我這樣的產品，這就是我閱讀所有這些規則的原因。下面沒有任何內容取決於此。每個數字都來自 Google 自己的頁面或公共軟體包註冊表，方法在最後。 11 月 24 日，Google 全面推出 Workspace MCP 伺服器，引入了兩個使用級別，並發布了 Workspace AI 工具附錄。公告中的核心規則是：代理「必須使用 MCP 存取 Workspace 數據，而不是直接呼叫 Workspace REST API」。技術執行將於 2027 年 2 月 1 日開始。隨之而來的一些好處是好的。外部代理必須在 OAuth 中識別自己的身份，以便管理員可以像管理任何其他應用程式一樣管理它們。管理員可以設定規則，讓使用者確認敏感操作、審核日誌中顯示的代理程式操作，以及在有人使用代理程式時套用現有的 DLP 規則。如果您看到提示注入讓代理轉發郵箱，您就會想要這一切。不過，這些都不需要授權或計量表。

代理身份是 OAuth 客戶端上的複選框，“將此客戶端用作人工智能驅動的代理”，Google 的幫助頁面將其稱為自我聲明。它在 REST 上的工作方式相同。無論哪種方式，審核日誌和 DLP 都在 Google 這邊運行。確認提示是唯一需要在協定中掛鉤的控件，這可能是類似於「我的組織中的代理必須使用 MCP」的管理設定。所以我研究了授權和定價本身的作用。代理商必須採取的路徑是唯一沒有免費配額的路徑 Workspace 現在有免費的標準層和付費的擴充層。在 Scaled 上，REST 流量為每個計費帳戶提供每日免費津貼：7,000 萬個 Light、1,000 萬個 Medium 和 100 萬個 Premium Gmail 請求，雲端硬碟和日曆也有類似的津貼。您只需支付高於該金額的費用。 Scaled 上的 MCP 根本沒有任何津貼。從 2027 年 4 月 1 日起，每個成功的 MCP 請求都會計費，當您升級時，標準版每天 5,000 個免費 MCP 請求將消失。還有一個內部使用例外，可以讓公司自己的專案無需付費即可獲得更高的 REST 配額。它不包括 MCP 。為自己的郵箱建立自己的代理的公司一旦超過每天的 5,000 個免費請求，就會在其工作區許可證之上按呼叫付費，而讀取相同郵箱的普通腳本則不需要。

基本電子郵件助理的費用是多少 免費的標準層將 MCP 的上限限制為每天每個項目、每個產品 5,000 個請求，由該項目的每個人共享。大多數 Gmail MCP 工具都算是一個請求。 search_threads 和 list_drafts 計為 10，因為它們在下面進行了多次呼叫。這使得整個專案每天的免費電子郵件搜尋量達到 500 次。 Google 的配額頁面也表示，失敗的工具呼叫將被計費，因為它們會傳回帶有錯誤標誌的 HTTP 200。 REST 計費僅計算成功的回應。為了了解這在實踐中意味著什麼，我模擬了一個謙虛的助手：每個工作日進行 5 次搜尋、15 次線索閱讀和 3 次草稿。也就是說，每人 68 個單位，因此有 73 人用完了免費套餐。在 Scaled 上，以 Google 的價格（搜尋和閱讀貼文都是高級版，每 1,000 人 0.50 美元），每人每月 0.73 美元。也就是說，500 人每月 364 美元，5,000 人每月 3,641 美元。在 REST 上，即使每次通話都按高級費率計費，在大約 43,000 人之前，相同的通話都不會產生任何費用。工作量是我的猜測。插入你自己的，間隙保持相同的形狀。公平地說，對於 Google 來說，這些金額很小，而且沒有人因為每人 0.73 美元而破產。問題在於結構：代理程式需要使用的路徑是儀表從第一次呼叫開始運行的路徑，運行儀表的公司也決定路徑上存在哪些工具。

在 Gmail 的 MCP 中，发送、回复和转发目前需要合作伙伴访问权限，并且一般不可用。 5 月 1 日，Google 开放了 Workspace MCP 服务器作为公共开发者预览版，并将 MCP 宣传为代理获取上下文和工具的标准方式。沒有要求。同一篇帖子还承诺现有项目的业主在配额变更前至少提前 60 天通知。谷歌的工具安全页面现已纳入美国

Anthropic and/or OpenAI, can you please throw your agents at my paper? - Wilsons Blog

Anthropic and/or OpenAI, can you please throw your agents at my paper?

So last week I wrote a blog post that did pretty well. Here’s the hackernews discussion:

It was popular enough to be picked up by a few newsletters, including the Financial Times Alphaville further reading (imagine my excitement when I saw ft.com coming up in my analytics).

Here’s the thing, the model and the graphs in there are based on a paper, that paper is currently in review at the Journal of Economic Modelling, but to be honest, I think it needs even more stress testing. If the conjecture posed in the conclusion of that paper is true, it’s a big deal. So now that Riemann is done, maybe we can leave the mathematicians alone for a bit? Maybe you could take that thousand agent swarm and throw it at something else? The paper is here:

If it turns out that the paper has some glaring omission or fault, that would be great, because then perhaps I could get a good nights sleep for the first time in a while (not because the conclusion is scary, quite the opposite, it gives me a lot of hope, but even an abundance of hope can keep oneself awake).

hn.originalTitle: LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you
hn.sourceOriginalText:
LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you | Michael Harley

In the evenings after work, I will often sit out back on the porch and do some phone rotting. That usually takes the form of me just flipping through reels on Instagram, allowing the algorithm to take me where it may. I usually pair this with a healthy tumbler of rum or bourbon. I'm turning my brain off after work, and I'm just having a good time on the internet. The kids might call it dopamine maxxing? Hell, I don't know. Who gives a shit about what those assholes would call it?

Anywho, I often encounter songs I really really like, and I would like to listen and discover more of please. Instagram makes it hard for me to connect with the band outside of their platform. I was trying to make this connection manually myself at first. I would just email myself a reel from my phone. Then when I'm back on the sofa and in the mood to track down new music, I'd open the reels and do my best to search on Bandcamp or YouTube or try to figure out if some of these musicians had a way to buy music from them. Very few do these days. They send you their Spotify link or send you to their TikTok page. I don't want to do any of that. I'd like to trade US dollars in exchange for some m.

So, I used Claude Code to build a skill that does this for me. It opens the Instagram reel and attempts to identify the artist and song. It then tries to determine if the artists have a Bandcamp page so I can purchase the songs I want, and if it finds one, it gives me the URL so I can click it to complete the trade I want. I want to buy music from artists who make music I like. That's a fair and wholesome endeavor, I feel, but this recently stopped working.

It turns out Bandcamp added a challenge on their search API page. Ah bummer. No worries, that was an unpublished workaround anyway. As I was mulling over this discovery, the robot went on to explain that it would not help me work around the challenge. cue Nick Young question marks

Well, that led me down a whole nother rabbit hole, which is turning into this post. There's another branch of my skill that attempts to locate the same song from the Instagram reel on YouTube, and it'll download the song to my computer if I ask.

So let me get this straight. The robot, which is my robot that I pay a pretty penny for, will not attempt to work around the challenge at Bandcamp so that I can more easily connect with bands to complete a sale, but it will download the YouTube song, which doesn't send any money to the band or anyone ???

This is the real danger of the frontier AI models. Not that it won't help me hack Bandcamp [1] , but that this model doesn't really work for us. Well, they do, but only insofar as Anthropic or OpenAI or whoever else allows them to. In this case, Anthropic is trying to ensure that people can't use their models for evil. I'm not trying to do evil. I'm actually trying to do good! I want to buy something from a small artist on the internet. That's basically the most wholesome thing a person can do on the internet!

Have no doubt, dear reader, these companies want to dominate. They want to capture the market. They want all the money. It'll be the same march to enshittification that happened with Google. A bunch of nerds who built something cool sold out, and it turned into just another business that decided to remove its don't be evil mantra.

Right now, I think the robots are providing real information to the best of their ability, but I think it's only a matter of time until we must wonder if the answers they're providing are real answers that the robot found, or if they're weighted answers Anthropic put there because a company gave it enough money for product placement. I want to know the best robot vacuum according to old reddit or other trusted sources like Wirecutter, weighed and measured according to what I, and thus my robot agent, think are important requirements. I don't want to know which robot vacuum parent multinational conglomerate has a large ad budget.

And it's not just ads. If Anthropic can tell its model not to work around a challenge, then it can tell its model to do whatever the US government tells it to do, including not helping people download copyrighted music. It does that some now, but it's easy to slip the noose on that. For now.

This is the reason I want a local model that runs in my homelab. My robot should work for me and have my best interests in mind, not the interests of US corporate copyright holders. I plan to study up on what "open models" even m

hn.sourceOriginalText:
AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp  | devnull.land

tl;dr — I recommend using llama-cpp-rdna-boosts if you have an AMD graphics card. It’s lean, and increased my token generation from 35 to 55 tokens/second, and my prefill from 700 to 1300 tokens per second. YMMV.

As of November 2026, an explosion in the number of bespoke inference engines has taken place. Many of them take inspiration from the engines that enabled much of the LLM inference up 'til now: llama.cpp, SGLang, vLLM, etc.

The rationale isn’t that those options are bad, but merely that they are generalist engines, optimized for no particular hardware and with a focus on broad compatibility. Others feel the development pace of those engines have slowed down, and with the help of LLMs, they can move faster on their own.

Some examples of these new inference engines* are Strata, Basalt, RustingStrata, etc…

These new forks generally all have a few things in common:

They focus on a specific subset of models and/or hardware

They use a frontier model to vibe-code the entire thing

They chase ever-higher token generation speeds

… and the results are stunning! Strata is able to run a heavily-quantized model of Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 180B parameter model , on a 16GB VRAM graphics card, and 16GB system RAM, and have it generate tokens at a surprisingly high rate.

In and of itself those three things are not red flags (the second is concerning, of course, but it may be SOP in a year’s time — who knows!), but as these projects have evolved, that relentless chase toward higher token generation speeds has taken an unfortunate turn, in that the optimizations are less about hardware-specific changes, but more about changing how the model thinks so that it goes brrr faster.

Strata specifically has taken to preferring to poll experts loaded in VRAM even if other experts (pushed to system RAM/disk) would have been normally chosen. This is just one example, but certainly not the last.

That said, I was fortunate to stumble upon yet another project that promised improvements, delivered, and was more aligned with my software development philosophy.

Enter llama-cpp-rdna-boosts . It is a repository that contains a minimal set of changes that you apply against a pinned commit of llama.cpp. It is in essence a fork, but one whose changeset is continually re-applied to newer versions of llama.cpp. It contains AMD-specific improvements that drastically improve prefill and token-generation speeds.

I appreciate llama.cpp’s approach to software development. They are a stable base to branch off from. Contributions are vetted throughly and applied judiciously. ✅

The rdna-boosts repo is a set of small patches that are applied to base llama.cpp. Fewer moving parts mean fewer things to maintain ✅

The changes are (somewhat opaquely, it’s all straight Claudish 😬) outlined in the documentation, ensuring some degree of transparency. ✅

If you have ROCm libraries installed on your system, you can build the image yourself. I didn’t want to mess with that, so I used the pre-built images published.

podman pull ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1

This sets up an image that you can run sandboxed via podman to launch the inference server:

podman run --rm -it \ --network=host \ --device /dev/kfd \ --device /dev/dri \ --group-add video \ -v "$HOME/models:/models" \ "ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1" \ My actual launch script passes a few additional flags, but those are the important lines.

I imagine upgrading would be pulling a new image down, though I have not tried this yet.

On my setup, an AMD R9700 connected to my laptop via an eGPU interface, this improved prefill and token generation rates when running ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_L) with MTP enabled:

Strata and its ilk were always promising the moon and it was never clear what steps they took to make that happen. I’m very much looking forward to what the rdna-boosts community come up with next.

* It’s worth noting that between these two groups, vllm-radiance made an appearance, which was a fork of vLLM with AMD-specific patches. I tried this too, but the build steps were so onerous and vLLM so overbuilt for my specific use case (1 machine, 1 developer), that I abandoned it and went back to vanilla llama.cpp

Strata is able to run a heavily-quantized model of Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 180B parameter model , on a 16GB VRAM graphics card, and 16GB system RAM, and have it generate tokens at a surprisingly high rate.

In and of itself those three things are not red flags (the second is concerning, of course, but it may be SOP in a year’s time — who knows!), but as these projects have evolved, that relentless chase toward higher token generation speeds has taken an unfortunate turn, in that the optimizations are less about hardware-specific changes, but more about changing how the model thinks so that it goes brrr faster. Strata specifically has taken to preferring to poll experts loaded in VRAM even if other experts (pushed to system RAM/disk) would have been normally chosen. This is just one example, but certainly not the last. That said, I was fortunate to stumble upon yet another project that promised improvements, delivered, and was more aligned with my software development philosophy. Enter llama-cpp-rdna-boosts . It is a repository that contains a minimal set of changes that you apply against a pinned commit of llama.cpp. It is in essence a fork, but one whose changeset is continually re-applied to newer versions of llama.cpp. It contains AMD-specific improvements that drastically improve prefill and token-generation speeds. I appreciate llama.cpp’s approach to software development. They are a stable base to branch off from. Contributions are vetted throughly and applied judiciously. ✅ The rdna-boosts repo is a set of small patches that are applied to base llama.cpp.

Fewer moving parts mean fewer things to maintain ✅ The changes are (somewhat opaquely, it’s all straight Claudish 😬) outlined in the documentation, ensuring some degree of transparency. ✅ If you have ROCm libraries installed on your system, you can build the image yourself. I didn’t want to mess with that, so I used the pre-built images published. podman pull ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1 This sets up an image that you can run sandboxed via podman to launch the inference server: podman run --rm -it \ --network=host \ --device /dev/kfd \ --device /dev/dri \ --group-add video \ -v "$HOME/models:/models" \ "ghcr.io/stew675/llama-cpp-rdna-boosts:server-rocm-10.1" \ My actual launch script passes a few additional flags, but those are the important lines. I imagine upgrading would be pulling a new image down, though I have not tried this yet. On my setup, an AMD R9700 connected to my laptop via an eGPU interface, this improved prefill and token generation rates when running ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_L) with MTP enabled: Strata and its ilk were always promising the moon and it was never clear what steps they took to make that happen. I’m very much looking forward to what the rdna-boosts community come up with next.

* It’s worth noting that between these two groups, vllm-radiance made an appearance, which was a fork of vLLM with AMD-specific patches. I tried this too, but the build steps were so onerous and vLLM so overbuilt for my specific use case (1 machine, 1 developer), that I abandoned it and went back to vanilla llama.cpp ← Back to all posts

hn.originalTitle: Show HN: An agent skill that optimizes code with falsifiable hypotheses
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Agentic Algorithm Engineering (AAE)

Agents that optimize your code like an algorithm engineer: a falsifiable hypothesis before every experiment, correctness checked after every change, one reviewable patch per accepted change, and a PDF report of the whole session.

A skill for Claude Code and Codex, from the Algorithm Engineering Group at Heidelberg University.

Results on established open-source codes

Every kept change was checked against the original output.

How it works: the Algorithm Engineering cycle

Algorithm Engineering is a cycle of design, analysis, implementation and experiment, driven by falsifiable hypotheses. AAE hands this cycle to an autonomous agent. During setup you agree with the agent on the benchmark, the metric, the correctness assertions and the budget; then it runs on its own.

A falsifiable hypothesis: "changing X will improve the metric by roughly Z, because ..."

Predict direction and size of the effect before measuring, from profiling and analysis.

A minimal change, committed to Git, with the correctness assertions checked.

Run the benchmark; keep the change only if it is better and still correct, otherwise revert.

From the report of the KaHIP kaffpa session: 122 experiments, 69 hypotheses, 41 patches, 3.9x faster in total.

/plugin install aae --marketplace CHSZLab/AgenticAlgorithmEngineering /aae:aae make the solver in src/ faster on the graphs in data/ In Codex, install the skill with scripts/install_codex_skill.py and call it with $aae ; any other agent can follow AAE.md . To try it first, run the 10-minute quick-start example : a slow but correct shortest-path program with a benchmark and a correctness check.

Sessions share what they learned: the knowledge base collects optimization techniques and experiment results, and agents read it before they start. Contributions from your own sessions are welcome.

David A. Bader, Adil Chhabra, Ernestine Großmann, Monika Henzinger, Alexander Noe, and Christian Schulz. Agentic Algorithm Engineering: Improving Shared-Memory Exact Minimum Cuts. In 13th DIMACS Implementation Challenge Workshop: Network Flows 2.0, OASIcs, 2027. To appear. Preprint: arXiv:2609.07204 .

hn.originalTitle: AI agents now control part of DeepMind's compute for Gemini experiments
hn.sourceOriginalText:
AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant

AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant

Google Deepmind lets AI agents run experiments on their own for the next Gemini model. On the company's podcast, VP of Research Koray Kavukcuoglu, who leads Gemini development, frames this as part of a strategic shift at the lab. Rather than running separate teams for specialized projects like AlphaFold and nuclear fusion, Deepmind now relies on a single general-purpose algorithm for both science and products, he says. Each Gemini generation, he adds, is a hand-built one-off rather than a fixed architecture, while parallel teams work on its successors.

According to Kavukcuoglu, AI agents control part of the compute themselves to run experiments, though the lab is still far from full recursive self-improvement. As a safety measure, Deepmind doesn't reward the agents' internal thought streams ("Chain of Thought") during training, he says, so their intentions stay unfiltered and reviewable in natural language before they act.

Kavukcuoglu also points to limits. Today's AI can depict physical processes such as fluid flows and collisions with visual accuracy, he says, but doesn't understand them precisely. No test can show when models will close those gaps and reach artificial general intelligence (AGI), he argues, because no benchmark captures the core of intelligence. In his view, AGI won't begin until useful everyday products earn enough trust for people to hand decisions over to them, the way they would when working with other people. Ad Ad
